newsitem.title: USA: Noxso to sell plant for $11 million.
newsitem.headline: Noxso to sell plant for $11 million.

text.p: Noxso Corp said Monday it signed a letter of intent to sell its liquid sulfur dioxide plant in Charleston, Tenn., to merchant bank Republic Financial Corp for $11 million.
The company, which is reorganizing under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code, said it constructed the plant on property owned by Olin Corp under a supply agreeement with Olin.
The company said the letter of intent sets September as target for the execution of a definitive agreement and November 1997 for the deal's closing.
A company spokeswoman was not immediately available to say whether the plant's sale would lead to job cuts.

Noxso said a definitive sale depends on negotiations with third parties of various associated agreements; completion of a contract for the sale of liquid SO2; the cooperation of Olin, which has been involved in a dispute with Noxso concerning the plant; and the bankruptcy court's approval.
Noxso's stock traded unchanged at $0.531250 Monday morning.
